To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fatigue lives of plasma-sprayed HA-coated Ti- 6Al-4 V are reduced when the coatings are subjected to a 400 degrees C post-deposition anneal in air, and that the reduction is due primarily to the stress-relieving effects of the treatment.

the post-deposition anneal treatment at low temperature (400 degrees C) was found to significantly increase the crystalline HA content of the coating, however, the coating was still amorphous after the treatment; the oxide layer thickness was found to decrease after the treatment; and the fatigue resistance of the Ti-6Al substrate was significantly reduced by the treatment.

the post-deposition heat-treatment of plasma-sprayed HA coatings at low temperatures (i.e., 400 degrees C) is an effective method of enhancing the crystallinity of HA and that this treatment can have a detrimental effect on the fatigue resistance of Ti-6Al-V substrates, particularly when used in conjunction with thick HA coatings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of post-spraying heat treatments of HA coatings on the fatigue behaviour of Ti-6Al4V substrates.
the effect of a low-temperature heat treatment on the crystallography, composition and thickness of the oxide layer and the fatigue behaviour.
understanding the effect of post-spraying thermal treatment on the structure, composition, and fatigue resistance of plasma-sprayed HA-coated Ti-4Al-6V substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 400 degrees C heat treatment did improve the HA coating, but not enough to overcome the effects of the stress-relief heat treatment.
the 90-h post-spraying treatment at 400 C in air was not an effective means of improving the fatigue resistance of plasma-sprayed HA coatings on Ti-6Al-V substrates.
the post-deposition heat-treatment of plasma-sprayed HA at 400 degreesC for 90h is not recommended for use in the present application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the post-deposition heat treatments used in this study were not effective at restoring fatigue life in Ti-6Al-V substrates with HA coatings.

the fatigue resistance of a Ti-6Al4-V substrate is significantly reduced by a 90-h annealing treatment at temperatures as low as 400 degrees C, and that a 90-h treatment is sufficient to cause significant recovery in the crystalline structure of a plasma-spray HA coating.
the post-deposition heat treatments at 400 degrees or 500 degrees C are not recommended for HA-coated Ti- 6Al-4 V, and that the as-spraying process should be used to produce the coatings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order for HA-coated Ti-64 to be used in a fatigue-critical application, it is essential that the substrate be stress relieved before coating deposition.
post-deposition heat treatments should be avoided in the production of Ti-6Al-V implants with HA coatings.

the post-deposition heat-treatment process can be used to improve the crystallographic properties of plasma-sprayed HA coatings without significantly affecting the fatigue resistance of the underlying substrate.
